question.prompt: When \(x^{13}+1\) is divided by \(x-1,\) the remainder is:

solutions.explanation:
Because \(x-1\) has degree \(1\), the remainder must be a constant, say \(r\). Polynomial division gives an identity
\[
x^{13}+1=(x-1)Q(x)+r
\]
for some polynomial \(Q(x)\).

Substituting \(x=1\) makes the entire quotient term vanish, leaving
\[
r=1^{13}+1=2.
\]
The remainder is \(\boxed{2}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
solutions.title: Make the quotient term vanish
